payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Change the image into pencil drawing
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is there image-grounded evidence of any progress toward rendering the content as a pencil drawing, even if the transformation is incomplete?
node.criteria: Pass if the image shows some visible pencil-drawing-style treatment of its content, including an incomplete treatment; fail if sufficient evidence shows no requested transformation has progressed; unknown if evidence is insufficient to determine whether any such progress occurred. Unrelated edits do not count as progress.
node.binding: Assess only visible changes in the supplied image that move its visual content toward a pencil-drawn style; do not infer progress from unrelated changes.

node_traces.evidence: The edited image shows a visible pencil-drawing-style treatment: colors are muted and the food and surrounding objects have sketch-like shading and outlines compared with the source.
The edited image shows a visible pencil-drawing-style treatment across the scene, with muted colors, grainy shading, and sketch-like outlines on the food and surrounding objects.
The edited image shows a visible pencil-drawing-style treatment: colors are muted and the food, dishes, and tableware have softened, sketch-like shading and texture compared with the source.

The edited image has a visible muted, grainy, pencil-like treatment across the food and surrounding objects, indicating progress toward a pencil drawing, though it retains substantial photographic color and detail.

The edited image has a visibly muted, gray-toned, grainy treatment across the food and surrounding objects, with softened, sketch-like shading consistent with some progress toward a pencil-drawing style.

fulfillment: The node’s completion criterion is too permissive and its binding is truncated/ambiguous: several runs call the image complete based on muted tones, grain, and sketch-like shading, while another identifies substantial photographic color, shading, and detail and correctly returns partial. In the edited image, the scene is desaturated and textured, but retains photographic lighting, smooth gradients, and realistic detail; those cues support progress, not by themselves a completed pencil drawing. Tighten the distinction between local/style progress and a whole-image result: require evidence that the scene reads as a drawing overall, and have the decision explicitly weigh remaining photographic appearance rather than treating generic grain or muted color as sufficient. Preserve partial when progress is established but the whole-image criterion fails; reserve unknown for genuinely unavailable evidence. The transport failure in one s3 trace is an execution/dependency failure, not negative visual evidence, and should remain unresolved rather than count as failure. Repeated yes/partial variation signals that the whole-image threshold and evidence standard need clearer calibration, not that the requested edit is absent.
s3: Clarify the binding’s truncated comparison and calibrate the pass threshold around the requested whole-image transformation. The edited image shows broad desaturation and grain/softening, but much of the scene still retains photographic lighting, gradients, and realistic detail; those cues indicate progress, not automatically a completed pencil drawing. Require the decision to weigh whether the overall image reads as a drawing, citing both drawing-like evidence and any substantial photographic appearance, rather than treating muted color or texture alone as sufficient. Keep partial available when visible progress exists but the whole-image criterion is not met; use unknown only when visual evidence is genuinely unavailable. Treat the transport failure as an execution failure, not negative visual evidence. Repeated pass/partial variation calls for a clearer evidence standard, not an assumption that the requested edit is absent.

Repair the typed binding/criteria so this support node answers only whether visible, image-grounded changes move the content toward pencil drawing; do not make it judge whether the whole image is fully transformed. Here, desaturation, softened shading, and grain across the scene support progress, while retained photographic lighting and realistic detail limit completion. Keep those judgments separate so this node’s pass does not imply overall fulfillment; let the downstream aggregate preserve partial when progress exists but the edit is incomplete. Do not treat muted color or generic grain alone as decisive—require drawing-like visual evidence and consider remaining photographic appearance. Keep unknown for genuinely insufficient visual evidence, and treat transport or dependency failures as unresolved execution issues, not negative visual evidence. Repeated pass/partial variation calls for clearer criterion boundaries, not a presumption that the requested edit is absent."}
